html:
The Colville are an Interior Salish people of the Columbia River around Kettle Falls in north-east Washington State. Kettle Falls was one of the great salmon fishing places of the Columbia, where many peoples gathered each summer. The Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Colvile nearby in 1825, named after one of its governors, and the name passed to the people.

In 1872 the United States set up the Colville Reservation, which brought together twelve tribes, among them the Colville, Nespelem, Sanpoil, Okanagan and Chief Joseph's band of Nez Perce. The Grand Coulee Dam drowned Kettle Falls in 1940 and ended the salmon runs above it.
